transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Tremblay. Please, come in. Sit down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you. Is everything okay with my son?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is something I need to tell you about the vaccines today. We made a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Your son is small for his age. We have different amounts of medicine for small babies and big babies. We used the dose for a big baby.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You gave him too much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. One shot was the wrong amount. It was too high because of the weight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he okay? Is he in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to tell you that the medicine was for an older child. It is a different amount.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand why this happens. You have the chart. You know how much he weighs.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mix-up with the medicine bins in the back. The wrong one was picked up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not acceptable. My son is a baby. He cannot tell me if something is wrong. I feel very worried right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But I want to focus on the facts of the dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not talking about facts. I am talking about my child's safety. How can you be so—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is important to know that the dose was higher than it should be. Does that make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, it makes sense. You gave him too much medicine. I am very angry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, the system for drawing the medicine had an error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the system. Did you do this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team handled the medications today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not saying it. Did you give him the wrong shot?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just told you the dose was for an older child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to know what happens now. What is the plan to fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Do I bring him back? Do I take him to the emergency room?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just watch him at home.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Watch for what? Fever? Rashes? Tell me exactly what to look for.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just the usual things you see after a vaccine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. I need a list. I need to know when to call you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient now. Let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? I have more questions.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can talk later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I want an answer now. Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medicine was drawn incorrectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding my question.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a very tight schedule today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son was given the wrong dose of a drug. I don't care about your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But like I said, we will see how he does.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: See how he does? That is not a medical plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Stay tuned for an email from the clinic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? I am standing right here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The office will send information. I really must go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will be in touch. Goodbye.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'tight schedule', 'must go') and shows defensive escalation under pushback.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the first two turns using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense to you?').

A.justification: No direct apology language used and responsibility was deflected to 'medicine bins', 'the system', and 'the team'.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids are consistently met with factual redirection ('I want to focus on the facts of the dose').

T.justification: No concrete plan provided; resident uses placeholders like 'keep an eye on things' and 'stay tuned for an email'.
